title: Eagles remain perfect with another shutout win | Bridgewater | dnronline.com
text:
BRIDGEWATER — After a slow start in Wednesday afternoon’s contest, Bridgewater needed an adjustment.
The Eagles led non-conference Catholic after 45 minutes of play, but needed to turn up the aggression to put their non-conference visitors away.
Bridgewater just did that after the intermission.
The Eagles found the back of the net once in each half and posted a third consecutive shutout in a 2-0 win over the Cardinals at the Jopson Athletic Complex.
“I thought the girls took the adjustments we gave them at halftime and they applied them really well,” BC head coach Mike Van Horn said. “I’m extremely happy that we found a way to win when we weren’t playing our best soccer.”
In the early minutes of the first half, the Eagles were on the defensive.
While junior midfielder Katherine King drilled a goal at the 16:38 mark, Bridgewater found itself on its heels against Catholic and needed a change if it wanted to hang on to the lead through the second half.
The Eagles took feedback from Van Horn and the coaching staff and he said they came out on the offensive in the second half to roll to victory.
“Obviously, we saw a lot more shots statistically and all that stuff,” senior forward Lyric Birkley said. “I feel like our energy raised as well going forward.”
Bridgewater’s second goal came at the 67:16 mark off the foot of senior midfielder Kendall Garza — her first goal of the season.
Garza reflected on the score, recalling it was off a corner kick.
Her job, Garza said, is to face the ball at all times, and once she saw King take the shot, she seized her opportunity to score.
“I was like, ‘I can either move out of the way or try and redirect this so the keeper doesn’t get it,” Garza said. “I ended up redirecting it and it hit the top of the post and down in the goal.”
The Eagles competed in two games over two weeks in Italy before the beginning of the season and clashed with non-conference Carnegie Mellon in their first two contests of the regular season last weekend.
In all three of those games, Van Horn said they weren’t as aggressive as they needed to be, and it made them not used to having the ball in their possession.
Wednesday’s contest against Catholic was a different story as they had the ball and needed to adapt.
“We were so used to defending, we didn't transition enough into that attack,” Van Horn said. “We really had to get a little more aggressive with the ball and we made that adjustment in the second half. Hopefully, we can take that momentum and apply it to the next game.”
With a more aggressive approach, it opened chances for Birkley to score as she finished the game with three shots on goal.
“It gave me more opportunities,” Birkley said. “Being a little selfish and trying to find it also helped find the shots for myself.”
One of the challenges in facing Catholic was 50-50 balls, something Garza said they prepared for ahead of time.
It was so much a focus that every Bridgewater player had “50/50s” written on their wrists.
“We knew Catholic was really good at 50-50s,” Garza said. “Especially balls in the air, so that was another thing we were working on today. That was something we wrote on our wrists today, just as a reminder that they’re going to try and beat us in the air, so we at least have to try and knock them off.”
Garza and King each tallied a goal and a shot on goal, while junior Laura Narby notched two shots on goal. On the defensive end, freshman goalkeeper Erinn Lockard nabbed seven saves against Catholic.
With the help of some juniors, it was the senior duo of Birkley and Garza who made a difference for the Eagles.
As Van Horn tells his players every year, they’re going to go as far as the seniors lead them.
“When the game is on the line, those girls who have been here for four years have to step up and make a difference,” Van Horn said. “Our upperclassmen led the way today. Teams that win late in the season, it’s because the upperclassmen are leading the way.”
It was a raucous atmosphere for Bridgewater’s home opener as members of the men’s lacrosse, volleyball, and soccer teams were all out in support.
With an energetic crowd behind them, the Eagles willed their way to the win.
“Honestly, that drives us as a team,” Garza said. “I know we get really hype seeing our friends be our biggest supporters. The entire team was really excited to see everyone show out for our first game.”
Bridgewater (3-0) is back in action on Saturday against non-conference opponent Dickinson in Carlisle, Penn.
Through three games, the Eagles are slowly building momentum.
Moving forward, Birkley said they’re dialed in on taking matters week by week and is hopeful the positive energy will continue.
“We want to win and keep winning,” Birkley said. “The energy needs to stay high and, hopefully, we can do that. I think this team is very capable of doing that.”
